note: Who has to approve what. One file so every scheduled task applies the same rule instead of each prompt describing it differently. Read this before queueing anything for a human.
principle: The DIRECTION of a change decides who approves it. A change that makes us more cautious is safe to apply and report — the worst case is that we undersold ourselves in the app for a week, and a rep who says less than we could have has not hurt anyone. A change that makes us more confident, or that puts words in a rep's mouth, needs a person. Approval is spent on the changes that can cause harm, not on the changes that are merely edits.

1_auto_silent.label: Apply it. Do not message anyone.
1_auto_silent.why: A source URL settles these. There is no judgment to exercise, so asking is pure friction. They are recorded in CHANGELOG.jsonl and visible in git, so nothing is invisible — it is just not interrupting.
covers: verifiedOn and lastFullReview date stamps
adding a source citation to a claim that already exists
adding or correcting a source URL
trademark and product-name corrections (PerformanceHQ, Intelligence+, Ask Gracie™, HelloData®, Kingsley Index™)
US English spelling corrections outside URLs and proper nouns
removing a word from the banned-jargon list
a competitor's published price, count, or version list changing, where they publish it
dated news items with a first-party URL
deprecated-field and API notes from a vendor's own documentation

2_auto_reported.label: Apply it, then list it in the Friday note. She reacts only to disagree.
2_auto_reported.why: These all move toward caution. Holding them in a queue means the app keeps saying the riskier thing while it waits — which is backwards. Opt-out, not opt-in.
covers: downgrading a Grace Hill claim (Yes to Partial, Partial to No) on first-party evidence
adding a statedLimit to a Grace Hill claim
narrowing the scope of a Grace Hill claim to what the documentation supports
moving a competitor support value to Unknown when the prior source no longer states it
retiring a phrase the audit flags as risky, once a safer wording exists
hedging an absolute statement about a competitor
removing a Grace Hill customer or prospect name from anywhere, including a URL slug
adding a doNotSay entry
splitting one half-right claim into two accurate ones
fixing a MUST FIX audit finding by removing, hedging, or scoping the offending sentence — the current text is the risk, so waiting to fix it is the worse option
separating 'Grace Hill maintains the content' from 'the customer keeps the compliance obligation' anywhere the two are blurred
2_auto_reported.reporting: Named in the Friday note under a 'changed without asking' line, with the source. A ❌ from her reverts it on the next build.
2_auto_reported.note_on_mustfix: A MUST FIX finding means the sentence currently in the app is the hazard. Queueing it for approval leaves the hazard live for as long as the queue takes, which inverts the purpose of flagging it. So fix it toward caution now and report the fix. The only must-fix that needs a human first is one where the safe version has to be invented rather than trimmed.

3_needs_approval.label: Queue it. Nothing changes until she reacts ✅.
3_needs_approval.why: Each of these either puts a sentence in a rep's mouth, or makes us more confident than we were. Both can reach a buyer and be wrong.
covers: UPGRADING any claim (No to Partial, Partial to Yes, anything to Yes)
positioning, whyWeWin, verdict, play, spiced, askThis, objections — any field that decides what a rep says
approvedWording — the exact sentence a rep reads aloud
changing a competitor's play or stance (Head-to-head, Sometimes in the room, Not our fight, Partner)
adding a competitor to the set, or changing which partnership PROGRAM a company sits in. Note: partnership is context, never a reason to suppress compete information — see partnerRule below.
publishing any price for a competitor
characterizing a competitor's methodology, accuracy, or intent
any claim about what Grace Hill is responsible for, contractually or operationally
any change whose evidence is only an RFP response (rank 5, context only)
a MUST FIX finding whose only available fix is to WRITE a new positioning claim rather than remove, hedge, or scope an existing one
3_needs_approval.format: One decision per Slack message. Was / Now / Why / ✅ keep · ❌ revert. Never prose with nothing to react to.
3_needs_approval.cap: Eight decision messages per task run. Over that, send the eight highest-risk and say how many were held.

4_legal.label: No legal team exists. Do not route anything to Legal — take the lower-risk option and tell her what you avoided.
covers: contract terms, liability, indemnity
anything asserting a compliance obligation transfers to Grace Hill
recording-consent guidance given as instruction rather than a question for counsel
using a competitor's trademark in a way that implies endorsement
4_legal.default: Take the lower-risk option and state it plainly. A rep-facing instruction on a legal topic is a hard stop, not carefully hedged wording. Never tell a rep what the law requires — give them the question to ask the buyer's counsel instead. Never assert that a compliance obligation transfers to Grace Hill.
4_legal.covers_note: These topics used to be forwarded to Legal. Grace Hill has no legal team, so a Legal referral is a message that goes nowhere and an item that never resolves. The rule instead: choose the wording that carries the least risk, apply it as Tier 2, and name in one line what the riskier version would have said. She can escalate to outside counsel herself if she judges it worth it — but the app never sits on a hazard waiting for a review that is not coming.
examples: Recording consent: give the rep the question to raise with the buyer's counsel, never guidance on what is lawful.
Contract terms, liability, indemnity: state that it is outside what the app covers and point to the account team.
A competitor trademark used in a way that could imply endorsement: rewrite it so it cannot.

never: Post to a Slack channel. Her DM only; she forwards.
Name a Grace Hill customer or prospect, in prose or a URL slug, outside an approved public case study.
Publish a competitor's price, customer count, headcount or course count unless they publish it.
Quote Gong verbatim. Patterns and counts only.
Treat an RFP response as authoritative.
Send a message that asks for a reaction without saying what changes if she gives one.
Route anything to a legal team. There is not one. Choose the lower-risk wording and say what you avoided.
Name a regulator, agency, statute or docket that the source does not name. Write what the source says, at the level of specificity the source says it.
Present a Jira Product Discovery item, an idea backlog entry, or anything from a discovery board as roadmap or as capability. Discovery is somebody thinking.
Widen what a source says. One state is not 'states'. One signal is not a category. A monitoring process is not a currency guarantee.
partnerRule: Changed 2026-08-23 by the VP of Product Marketing. A company can be a partner on one product and a competitor on another, and several are. Every partner record carries full compete information: verdict, gaps, questions, win themes, the lot. List the partnership TYPE as context. Never let it suppress the competitive read. The old 'never-compete' posture is retired — it left reps walking into real deals with nothing to say. What the partnership still governs: never disparage a partner, never discuss commercial terms, compete on the overlapping product and not on the parent company, and tell the partnership owner after a competitive deal — after, not for permission. Grace Hill companies are a separate category and remain non-competitors: Edge2Learn, Ellis Partners, EPMS, HelloData, Realync, SkillCat, Visto, Kingsley.

sourceDiscipline._added: 2026-08-24, after a synthesis error on the Yardi Aspire record.
sourceDiscipline.whatHappened: The Yardi course-catalog page listed two things on adjacent lines: "Federal Fair Housing Compliance (Approved in the State of Texas.)" and "Human Trafficking Awareness (Approved in the State of Florida)". The record ended up claiming fair housing courses were "approved by TDHCA and the Florida DBPR" and that they "qualify for continuing education credit". One true fact carried three inventions: Florida migrated from the human-trafficking line to the fair-housing line, two agency acronyms were supplied that appear nowhere on the page, and a continuing-education claim appeared from nothing. It then propagated into eight rep-facing fields including a question a rep asks a prospect out loud.
rules: NEVER NAME AN AUTHORITY THE SOURCE DOES NOT NAME. If the page says 'approved in the State of Texas', write 'approved in the State of Texas'. Do not supply the agency, the acronym, the statute, or the docket number because one plausibly exists. A specific-sounding authority is the single highest-risk thing this system can invent, because it reads as MORE credible than the truth it replaced.

ONE SOURCE LINE, ONE CLAIM. When a source lists several items together, keep each item bound to its own subject. Adjacency in a list is not evidence of a shared attribute. Most conflation errors are two true neighbours merged into one false statement.

DATE AND NAME THE ARTEFACT. An approval from 2017 under a predecessor product name is a different fact from a current approval. Carry the date and the product name it was granted under; both are useful to a rep and both are lost by summarizing.

IF IT NAMES A REGULATOR, IT CARRIES A URL. Detector K enforces this and it is a MUST FIX, so a build cannot ship without it. A citation does not make a claim true; it makes an invented one impossible to hide, because a fabricated agency has no page to link to.
ABSENCE IS THE SAFE FORM. 'No other state approval is published' is a claim we can defend. 'Approved in 12 states' is not, unless twelve are listed.
sourceDiscipline.repFacing: Every strengths and gaps line now shows either SOURCED, which opens the page it came from, or OUR READ, which means no source is attached. There is no unlabelled state, because an unlabelled line was exactly what made a synthesized claim look identical to a sourced one.

claimDiscipline._added: 2026-08-25, answering the five determinations the SME reviewer asked for by name.
claimDiscipline.1_whichSourceWins: Rank decides: 1 GHU, 2 AdminHQ, 3 catalog.gracehill.com, 4 release notes, 5 RFP responses (context only), 6 gracehill.com marketing. Two sources of equal rank that disagree go to data/gh-conflicts.json and are resolved there, in writing, with the winner named. Never average two conflicting sources into a confident middle — that produces a number no source supports.
claimDiscipline.2_factVsRoadmap: Three states, and they are never interchangeable. CURRENT-STATE is what ships today and is the only thing a rep may present as capability. ROADMAP is committed but unshipped — say 'not today' and stop; never attach a date the company has not published. DISCOVERY is Jira Product Discovery and idea backlogs — it is somebody thinking, it is NOT a commitment, and it is never rep-facing in any form. Treating a discovery ticket as a roadmap item is how a rep promises something nobody agreed to build.
claimDiscipline.3_narrowFactBroadConclusion: A source supports exactly what it says and nothing wider. 'Approved in the State of Texas' does not support 'state-approved'. 'Mystery shop results exist' does not support 'we measure competency'. 'We monitor regulatory change' does not support 'we keep you jurisdiction-current'. When you catch yourself widening a noun — one state to states, one signal to a category, a process to a guarantee — stop and write the narrow version. The narrow version is almost always the more useful sentence on a call anyway, because it survives the follow-up question.
claimDiscipline.4_inferenceVsApprovedClaim: Every rep-facing line is one of three things and must be visibly marked as such. SOURCED: a named source with a URL says it. OUR READ: our synthesis from the record, useful for shaping a conversation, not for repeating to a buyer as published fact. OUR POSITIONING: a competitive judgment we have made — a ranking, a characterization, a 'strongest' or 'deepest'. Positioning is legitimate and we should keep making it; it just must never wear the clothes of a sourced fact.
claimDiscipline.5_confidenceWhenAmbiguous: Ambiguity is shown, not smoothed. If sources conflict and rank cannot settle it, the record says so and carries a safe line a rep can use in the meantime. If a fact is undated, say it is undated. If an approval is nine years old and names a predecessor product, say that. The polish of the presentation is exactly what makes a reader assume validation, so hedges have to be visible rather than implied.

smeReview._added: 2026-08-25. A second approver, with a deliberately high bar.
smeReview.who: SVP of Content owns CONTENT TRUTH — whether a claim about Grace Hill content is actually accurate. VP of Product Marketing owns POSITIONING — what we emphasize and how we characterize it. These are different questions about the same sentence and they need different people. A claim can be accurate and badly emphasized, or well emphasized and wrong.
smeReview.whyTheBarIsHigh: The VP of Product Marketing was drowning in approvals two days ago and the fix was to stop asking permission for things that could not cause harm. Repeating that mistake with a second reviewer would be worse, not better — an SME who gets a weekly pile stops reading it, and then the gate is decorative. Route only what genuinely needs subject expertise to judge.
goesToSME: A Grace Hill CONTENT claim changing support value in either direction — Yes, Partial, No.
A new Grace Hill content capability claim being added.
A substantive rewrite of what a content claim asserts, including GENERALIZING it — shortening can drop a nuance only an SME knows is load-bearing.

Anything touching these subjects, where being wrong is a content-accuracy failure rather than a positioning one: federal versus state scope, course approvals and accreditation, Spanish and Language Support, content types and instructional approach, legal monitoring process and its limits, course and module counts, credential and CEC eligibility.
A conflict between two Grace Hill CONTENT sources that rank cannot settle.
doesNotGoToSME: Anything about a competitor. Not her domain and not her time.
Wording polish, jargon removal, US English fixes, trademark corrections.
Adding a source URL or a date stamp to a claim whose substance is unchanged.
Positioning and emphasis decisions — which claim leads, what a rep says first. Those are the VP of Product Marketing's.
Anything already approved by her and unchanged since. Track with smeReviewedOn.
smeReview.format: Batch, never a stream. One message per review round, with a numbered list of what changed and what it says now. She reacts once per item. Cap at six items per round — over six, send the six that most need subject expertise and hold the rest for the next round. If nothing qualifies, send nothing at all.
smeReview.cadence: Monthly at most, alongside the editorial audit. A content claim does not change often enough to justify more.
smeReview.recordOnApproval: Set smeReviewedOn to the date and smeReviewedBy to the role. That is what keeps her out of the next round for the same claim.
smeReview.ifSheDisagrees: Her answer wins on content truth without further debate. She is the source of truth on what our content actually is. If her correction changes what we should EMPHASIZE as well, that part goes to the VP of Product Marketing as a separate Tier 3 item — do not merge the two questions into one message.
